newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX copper ended lower Wednesday, on moderate volumes, in line with LME copper, as the market gave back a little more of last week's gains.

"It really wasn't too significant a day, but there was some buying at the lows and some bidding for LME Long Beach (warehouse) warrants, probably reflecting Far East demand," Iceni Commodities trader Tony Ellis said.
COMEX May copper ended down 1.80 cents at 108.85 cents, after trading a 110.95-108.10 range. Estimated total volume for COMEX copper futures was 10,000 lots.
Wednesday's downmove still looks to be a correction in the four-month old uptrend which took copper to eight month highs last week, analysts said.

But the COMEX May/July backwardation slipped further to 3.00 cents from 3.30 cents Tuesday, while the LME cash-to-three month spread was steady around $64.00 a tonne, after slipping back from highs above $300 a tonne in recent weeks, suggesting seasonal demand and prompt market tightness is easing, traders said.

Smaller-than-expected LME inventory declines recently have dampened bullish sentiment, analysts said, but LME copper stocks at 205,525 are still below the recent highs of 275,275 tonnes seen last August and the end-March 1996 total of 345,000 tonnes.
Japanese purchases for tariff-free GSP imports of around 50,000 tonnes ahead of the April 1 deadline should prove to be a near-term supportive factor also, analysts said.
